content:
Work modulo \(503\) in the quotient ring
\[
R=\mathbb F_{503}[x]/(x^{502}-1).
\]

The image of \((1+x)^{10000}\) in \(R\) is
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{10000}\binom{10000}{k}x^k
=\sum_{r=0}^{501}S_r x^r,
\]
because exponents are reduced modulo \(502\).

Now write
\[
10000=19\cdot 503+443.
\]
Since \(503\) is prime,
\[
(1+x)^{503}\equiv 1+x^{503}\pmod{503}.
\]
Therefore
\[
(1+x)^{10000}
\equiv (1+x^{503})^{19}(1+x)^{443}\pmod{503}.
\]
In \(R\), we have \(x^{502}=1\), so \(x^{503}=x\). Hence
\[
(1+x)^{10000}\equiv (1+x)^{19}(1+x)^{443}
=(1+x)^{462}.
\]

Thus
\[
S_r\equiv
\begin{cases}
\dbinom{462}{r}\pmod{503},&0\le r\le462,\\[2mm]
0\pmod{503},&463\le r\le501.
\end{cases}
\]

For \(0\le r\le462\), none of the integers \(1,2,\dots,462\) is divisible by \(503\), so
\[
\binom{462}{r}=\frac{462!}{r!(462-r)!}
\]
is not divisible by \(503\).

Therefore exactly the \(39\) values \(S_{463},S_{464},\dots,S_{501}\) are multiples of \(503\). Hence the answer is
\[
\boxed{39}.
\]
